name: Bromantane (Ladasten)

b.x: 90.8% of 728 patients were rated as responders on the CGI-I scale. That number comes from an uncontrolled Russian multicenter study of asthenic disorders [1], with no placebo arm, at 50 to 100 mg daily over 28 days. Adverse events hit only 3% of participants. A separate placebo-controlled trial in neurasthenia found faster and larger symptom relief than placebo [6]. Bromantane (N-(4-bromophenyl)adamantan-2-amine, also sold as Ladasten) sits on an adamantane scaffold, the same carbon cage behind amantadine and memantine. Russia registered it in 2008 for asthenic conditions and neurasthenia. The compound first hit international radar when athletes at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics tested positive for it. What separates bromantane from stimulants like modafinil or amphetamines is the mechanism. It doesn't block dopamine reuptake. It doesn't dump monoamines into synapses. Instead, it upregulates tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) and aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AAAD), the two rate-limiting enzymes in dopamine production. In rats, a single dose more than doubled TH mRNA in the hypothalamus within 1.5 to 2 hours [4]. The result is a gradual, sustained lift in dopamine synthesis rather than a spike and crash. Community experience across several hundred documented reports on r/nootropics and peptide forums lines up closely with the clinical data. Users consistently describe calm energy, improved task initiation, and better physical stamina. Effects build over the first week; judging bromantane after a single dose misses the point entirely. Western clinical evidence is thin. No FDA-reviewed trials exist. No English-language double-blind placebo-controlled studies have been published. Most pharmacological data traces back to Russian-language journals or preclinical animal work. That gap is real, and it matters for anyone weighing risk.

Bromantane's primary action is indirect genomic upregulation of dopamine biosynthesis. It increases transcription of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) mRNA and protein in the hypothalamus, striatum, ventral tegmental area, and nucleus accumbens. It also upregulates aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AAAD), the enzyme converting L-DOPA into dopamine. Together, these increases produce more dopamine without the reuptake inhibition or vesicular dumping of traditional stimulants. The timeline matters. In rats, TH mRNA in the hypothalamus more than doubles within 1.5 to 2 hours of a single dose [4]. Those rat studies used 50 mg/kg by mouth [2]. This genomic mechanism is why effects build over days of consistent dosing. It also accounts for the low abuse potential; there's no immediate dopamine surge, just a steady upward shift in baseline synthesis capacity. On the anxiolytic side, bromantane strengthens GABA-ergic neurotransmission. The exact molecular target hasn't been fully characterized. It doesn't appear to act on GABA-A benzodiazepine binding sites directly. So you get anxiolytic properties without the sedation, cognitive fog, or dependence risk tied to benzodiazepines. Bromantane also increases expression of BDNF and NGF in certain brain regions (animal data). Those neurotrophic effects could contribute to the cognitive improvements reported with longer use, though human confirmation is sparse. Pharmacokinetically, oral bioavailability sits at approximately 42%. Peak plasma hits around 2.75 hours in females, roughly 4 hours in males. The compound is highly lipophilic and distributes into adipose tissue, which is why its primary metabolite (6-beta-hydroxybromantane) shows up in urine for up to two weeks after a single dose.
Bromantane benefits center on sustained dopaminergic drive and calm focus without stimulant-class side effects.
Upregulates TH and AAAD enzymes to increase dopamine production at the source, rather than depleting existing stores the way amphetamines do. This distinction matters for long-term use.

Combines mild stimulant and anxiolytic effects in one compound. Users consistently describe calm energy without jitteriness, a profile distinct from modafinil (tunnel vision) and racetams (purely cognitive).

Improved physical work capacity and endurance under stress. Bromantane was developed as an actoprotector, a drug class designed to boost physical output without the metabolic cost of classical stimulants [3].
Rapid onset with long-lasting activity. In rats, TH gene activity rises within 1.5 to 2 hours of one dose [4]. Community reports describe effects lasting 8 to 12 hours.
No tolerance or dependence observed at 50 to 100 mg daily in available clinical and community data. The Russian 28-day trial confirmed consistent efficacy throughout the cycle.
Raised BDNF and NGF gene expression in rat brain after a single dose [5], a possible neuroplasticity effect not yet tested in humans.

Large uncontrolled multicenter study (728 patients with asthenic disorders, no placebo arm) reported 90.8% CGI-I responders [1]. A smaller placebo-controlled neurasthenia trial found bromantane superior to placebo [6]. Mechanism (TH/AAAD upregulation → dopamine synthesis) is well-characterized in preclinical models. All clinical evidence from Russian-language publications. No independent replication in Western trials. Long-term safety data (beyond 28-day cycle) absent from controlled data. No dose-ranging RCT comparing 50 mg vs 100 mg outcomes. Zero new PubMed publications 2024-2026.

Both science and community converge on 50-100 mg/day oral dosing. Clinical efficacy matches community reports of improved energy, motivation, and stress tolerance. Community cycling pattern (4 weeks on/off) aligns with clinical trial duration (28 days). No significant divergence in dose or expected benefits.

Bromantane is oral. No reconstitution, no syringes, no bacteriostatic water. You're working with either pre-made capsules or raw powder. If you're dosing raw powder, a milligram-accurate scale (0.001 g resolution) is non-negotiable. A kitchen scale won't cut it for 25 to 50 mg doses. Weigh each dose individually or pre-weigh a batch into gelatin capsules. Pre-measured research-chemical capsules eliminate the weighing hassle. Capsule dosing accuracy depends entirely on the manufacturing process; always check the third-party COA. A small fatty meal before dosing may improve absorption. Bromantane's oral bioavailability is roughly 42% with significant first-pass metabolism. Fat helps lipophilic compounds cross the gut lining. Morning dosing only. The 8 to 12 hour activity window means anything after noon puts your sleep at risk. Start at 25 mg for the first week. Don't judge effects until day 7 at minimum; the TH/AAAD genomic mechanism takes time to ramp. Cycle 4 weeks on, 2 to 4 weeks off. The cycling isn't about tolerance (clinical data shows none) but about lipophilic accumulation in adipose tissue.
Cycling Protocol

The Russian label sets a 2-4 week course (Vidal), and the 728-patient study dosed for 28 days (PMID 21322821). Neither sets a break length. The 3 weeks off shown here is the middle of the 2-4 weeks off that community reports describe. Some users run shorter 2-week cycles. Due to lipophilic accumulation in adipose tissue, taking breaks is important even though acute tolerance doesn't appear to develop. Avoid stacking with other dopaminergic compounds during use.
Bromantane (Ladasten) Cycle

Primary cycling rationale is lipophilic tissue accumulation, not receptor desensitization or hormonal axis suppression. Bromantane distributes extensively into adipose tissue due to high lipophilicity. With daily dosing, tissue levels build throughout a 4-week cycle. Extended continuous use risks progressive accumulation, particularly hepatic, beyond what the 28-day clinical trial safety data covers. Secondary rationale: the main Russian studies ran 28 days (PMID 21322821, PMID 19491814), and the Russian label sets a 2-4 week course. Clinical data shows no acute tolerance development.

The biggest safety gap with bromantane is the absence of long-term controlled data. The Russian multicenter trial [1] ran for 28 days in 728 patients at 50 to 100 mg daily. Adverse events appeared in roughly 3% of participants. That's a reassuring number, but 28 days tells you nothing about what happens at month three or month six. Insomnia is the most commonly reported side effect, both in clinical data and across community forums. Bromantane's 8 to 12 hour duration of action means afternoon dosing reliably disrupts sleep. This complaint appears dose-independent; even 25 mg taken too late causes problems. The fix is straightforward: dose before 9:00 AM. Headache and tension surface mainly above 100 mg. At standard doses (50 to 100 mg), headaches are occasional and generally resolve with hydration. Users pushing to 150 mg report tension headaches as a consistent limiter. Paradoxical anxiety has been flagged by a subset of community users at doses exceeding 100 mg. The anxiolytic effect inverts in some individuals when dopaminergic tone gets too high. Reducing the dose resolves this. GI discomfort (loose stools, mild nausea) appears at higher doses. Mild dry mouth is reported intermittently. Mydriasis (pupil dilation) occurs at standard doses in some users. It's a marker of dopaminergic activity, not a safety concern, but it can cause photosensitivity. Hepatic strain is a theoretical risk. Bromantane is highly lipophilic and undergoes extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism. It accumulates in adipose tissue throughout a cycle. Liver enzymes (ALT, AST, GGT) should be checked at baseline and at the end of each 4-week cycle, particularly at the 100 mg dose. Any elevation beyond 2x the upper limit of normal warrants stopping. The compound's lipophilicity also means metabolites (primarily 6-beta-hydroxybromantane) remain detectable in urine for up to two weeks after a single dose. WADA lists bromantane as a non-specified stimulant (S6.A), prohibited in competition. Athletes under WADA rules can't have it in their system at events. Skin rash is listed in available data but frequency is unclear. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: no reproductive safety data exists. Children under 18 have not been studied. Anyone with severe hepatic impairment, known hypersensitivity to adamantane-class compounds, or active psychotic disorders should avoid bromantane. Stop use and consult a physician if you experience persistent insomnia despite early dosing, skin rash, mood instability, or any signs of liver strain.
Common Issues & Solutions

Insomnia: Take no later than 8:00-9:00 AM. The 8-12 hour activity window is dose-independent: afternoon dosing consistently disrupts sleep. If morning-only dosing still causes insomnia, reduce to 25 mg.
No noticeable effects in week 1: Expected: TH/AAAD genomic upregulation takes 5-7 days of consistent dosing. Do not increase dose based on week-1 assessment; wait until week 2 to evaluate.
Headache or tension: Most common above 100 mg. Reduce to 50-75 mg. Ensure adequate hydration. Headache at 50 mg indicates individual sensitivity: taper to 25 mg.
Paradoxical anxiety: Reported by some users at doses above 100 mg. Reduce dose immediately. Bromantane's anxiolytic effects can invert in sensitive individuals at high dopaminergic tone.
Mydriasis (pupil dilation): Documented at standard doses. No clinical action required, but relevant if photosensitivity is an issue. Indicates dopaminergic activity and does not warrant stopping.

Bromantane is not approved by the FDA for any indication. No US application for it appears in Drugs@FDA. Russia registered it as Ladasten in 2008 (certificate LSR-010257/08) for asthenic conditions and neurasthenia. It is sold there by prescription. In the United States, bromantane is sold as a research compound. It's not a controlled substance under the Controlled Substances Act, but it has no regulatory pathway for human therapeutic use. It cannot be marketed for human consumption. WADA lists bromantane as a non-specified stimulant (S6.A) on the 2026 Prohibited List. Like every S6 stimulant, it is prohibited in competition. Metabolites are detectable in urine for up to two weeks after a single dose. WADA's in-competition period generally starts at 11:59 p.m. the day before a competition and runs until the competition and its sample collection end. A dose taken days before that window can still show up in the test. Bromantane is not available through US compounding pharmacies, as it is not an approved compounding ingredient. faqs.a: Bromantane (Ladasten, CAS 87913-26-6) is a synthetic adamantane derivative with combined anxiolytic and psychostimulant properties. An uncontrolled Russian multicenter study of 728 patients with asthenic disorders reported 90.8% CGI-I responders at 50-100 mg daily over 28 days (PMID 21322821). It is approved in Russia but not by the FDA.

faqs.q: What is the recommended bromantane dosage?
faqs.a: Beginner: 25 mg oral daily. Moderate: 50 mg daily. Aggressive: 100 mg daily. Take in the morning; the 11-hour half-life means evening dosing can disrupt sleep. Russian clinical protocols used 50-100 mg for 28-day courses. Community users often cycle 4 weeks on, 2-4 weeks off.

Bromantane upregulates tyrosine hydroxylase expression, the rate-limiting enzyme in dopamine synthesis. Rather than releasing existing dopamine stores (like amphetamines), it increases production capacity. It also modulates GABA-ergic transmission, which accounts for the anxiolytic component. This dual mechanism is why it doesn't produce the crash or dependency profile of traditional stimulants.

faqs.q: What are the side effects of bromantane?
faqs.a: The Russian clinical data reports a favorable safety profile at 50-100 mg. Community-reported effects include mild headache, occasional GI discomfort, and vivid dreams. No dependency or withdrawal has been documented. The IOC banned bromantane after several athletes tested positive at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics. WADA, founded in 1999, lists it today as a non-specified stimulant (S6.A), prohibited in competition. Hepatotoxicity data is limited; liver panel monitoring is advised for cycles beyond 4 weeks.

faqs.q: Does Bromantane (Ladasten) need to be reconstituted?
faqs.a: No. Bromantane (Ladasten) is taken by mouth and is not reconstituted with bacteriostatic water.

faqs.q: What is the half-life of Bromantane (Ladasten)?
faqs.a: The half-life of Bromantane (Ladasten) is ~11 hours. This determines how frequently you need to dose for consistent blood levels.
